name: Railway
tagline: Projects, services, deploys, and logs your agent can manage on Railway.
description: Railway's hosted MCP server lets agents list and create projects, redeploy services, manage feature flags, and hand multi-step debugging to the Railway agent. The GraphQL API and the `railway` CLI cover the rest of the platform: variables, domains, volumes, environments, and logs.

methods.label: OAuth 2.0
methods.note: The hosted MCP server uses OAuth; you pick which workspaces and projects the client can reach.

methods.label: Account or workspace token
methods.note: Created at railway.com/account/tokens; sent as a Bearer token to the GraphQL API.

methods.label: Project token
methods.note: Scoped to one environment of one project; uses the Project-Access-Token header, not Bearer. The MCP server rejects it.

auth.guide:
**MCP with OAuth (easiest):** add `https://mcp.railway.com` in an OAuth-capable client and approve the workspaces and projects it may access.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http railway https://mcp.railway.com
```

**MCP through the CLI:** with Railway CLI 5.44.0 or later, `railway login` once, then let the CLI configure your editor. It proxies to the same server and reuses the CLI session, so no token lands in the editor config. `railway mcp local` runs the server in-process for machines that can't reach `mcp.railway.com`.

```bash
railway login && railway setup agent
```

**Account or workspace token (GraphQL):** create one at [Account → Tokens](https://railway.com/account/tokens). Leave the workspace on "No workspace" for an account token, or pick one to scope it.

```bash
curl https://backboard.railway.com/graphql/v2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RAILWAY_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"query { me { name email } }"}'
```

Project tokens (from project settings) use a `Project-Access-Token` header instead of Bearer and do not work with the MCP server. Auth failures can come back as HTTP 200 with an `errors` array.

interfaces.name: Railway MCP
interfaces.note: Also reachable over stdio through the CLI (`railway mcp`, set up with `railway setup agent`), which reuses the `railway login` session. `railway mcp local` runs a local server with a wider tool set (variables, domains, volumes, logs, metrics) for machines that can't reach mcp.railway.com. Project tokens are rejected; the server needs a user identity.

interfaces.name: Railway Public API
interfaces.note: Account, workspace, and OAuth tokens use Bearer. Project tokens use `Project-Access-Token: {token}` instead. Authorization failures can return HTTP 200 with an `errors` array.

interfaces.name: railway
interfaces.note: For CI, set RAILWAY_TOKEN to a project token or RAILWAY_API_TOKEN to an account or workspace token instead of logging in.
